Kumar Vikrant @ Dr. Kumar Vikrant vs The State Of Bihar on 11
January, 2024

Author: Anjani Kumar Sharan
Bench: Anjani Kumar Sharan
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna
 Criminal Miscellaneous No.84182 of 2023
 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-90 Year-2021 Thana- Mahila P.S. Distr

sentences.text:
======================================================
 Kumar Vikrant @ Dr. Kumar Vikrant S/O Ravi Narayan Rai R/O

Raja Bazaar
 Main Road, In Front Of Ram Janki Mandir,P.S- Balua, Distt.- East
 Champaran.

... 
 Versus  1. THE STATE OF BIHAR  2. Sneh Sanjay, w/o Kumar Vikrant @ Dr. Kumar Vikrant, D/o Sri Sanjay  Kumar Kaudilya, at present residing at Chandramani Bhawan, Street of T.
 College, Near- Govt. High School, Chiraiya Tand, P.S.- Kankarbagh, Dist  Patna  ... ...

Opposite Party/s  ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Madhurendra Kumar  For the Opposite Party/s : Mr.Raj Kishor Singh  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANJANI KUMAR SHARAN  ORAL ORDER 2 11-01-2024 Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State.
2. The petitioner apprehends his arrest in a case registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 494, 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Petitioner, who is husband of opposite party no. 2, is said to have ousted the opposite party no. 2 from her matrimonial home in association of his family members over the dowry demand and performed second marriage.
4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is an innocent person and has committed no offence.
Petitioner has neither made any dowry demand nor Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.84182 of 2023(2) dt.11-01-2024 drove her out of her matrimonial home nor tormented her over the demand of dowry.

The petitioner has relied upon the judgment of this Court Kumar Vikrant @ Dr. Kumar Vikrant vs The State Of Bihar on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159520209/
1 in the case of Md. Naimul Haque Ansari @ Naimul Haque Ansari @ Ors. Vs. The State of Bihar,
reported in 2006 (3) PLJR 182.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In that view of the matter, let the above named petitioner, be released on bail, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of six weeks from today, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Court below where the case is pending/successor Court in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 90 of 2021, subject to the condition as laid down under Section 438 (2) of the Cr.P.C.
6.

If so advised, either of the parties will be at liberty to make an application before the learned Court below for referring the matter to the District Mediation Centre for the purpose of reconciliation or for one time settlement.
7. Accordingly, this application stands disposed of.

(Anjani Kumar Sharan, J) Ranjeet/-
